'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**At least six [[park ranger]]s in the [[Virunga National Park]] in [[Rutshuru]], [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], are killed in an [[ambush]]. A [[Mai-Mai]] militia is suspected to have committed the attack. [https://www.barrons.com/news/at-least-six-dr-congo-park-rangers-killed-in-attack-01610288103?tesla=y (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
*[[Tigray War]]
**The [[Ethiopian National Defense Force]] says that it has killed 15 members of the [[Tigray People's Liberation Front]], including the [[Tigray Region|region]]'s former deputy police commissioner, and captured eight others, including the region's former president [[Abay Weldu]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-ethiopia-conflict/ethiopian-military-says-it-killed-15-members-of-rebellious-tigray-forces-captured-8-others-idUSKBN29F0JF (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**[[Professional Golfers' Association of America|PGA of America]] announces it will terminate an agreement to play the [[2022 PGA Championship|2022]] [[PGA Championship]] at [[Trump National Golf Club Bedminster|Trump National Golf Club]] in [[Bedminster, New Jersey|Bedminster]] because conducting the golf tournament there would have been "detrimental" to the PGA brand. [https://www.espn.com/golf/story/_/id/30689392/2022-pga-championship-leaving-trump-national (ESPN)]
**Payment processor [[Stripe (company)|Stripe]] will no longer process payments for the campaign website of [[President Donald Trump]] because of the company's policies against encouraging violence. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/stripe-stops-processing-payments-for-trump-campaign-website-11610319116 (''Wall Street Journal'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Sriwijaya Air Flight 182]]
**[[Indonesia]]n authorities locate the [[Flight recorder|black box]]es of the [[Sriwijaya Air]] [[Boeing 737-500]] PK-CLC that crashed into the sea soon after taking-off from [[Jakarta]], as human body parts and debris from the plane are found. Loss of everyone onboard is considered almost certain. [https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20210110-authorities-locate-black-boxes-retrieve-debris-after-indonesia-plane-crash (France 24)] [http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2021/01/10/rescuers-find-human-remains-after-deadly-sriwijaya-air-crash-.html (''The Jakarta Post'')]
*Gold mine [[explosion]] in [[Shandong]], [[China]].
**Twenty-two workers are trapped in a gold mine in [[Qixia, Shandong|Qixia]], east China's Shandong province after an explosion tore through the mine at 2:00 p.m. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2021-01/13/c_139665307.htm (''Xinhua News'')] [https://www.scmp.com/news/china/article/3117577/chinese-rescuers-race-save-22-trapped-gold-mine-blast (''South China Morning Post'')]
*Power is restored in [[Pakistan]] following a nationwide [[power outage|blackout]]. [https://www.ft.com/content/47c4ca69-918c-4cc2-bdcd-38849a6bec73 (''The Financial Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Crime in Australia]]
**A mother and her three daughters are found dead in a house fire in [[Glen Waverley, Victoria|Glen Waverley]], [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]]. Police are investigating it as a possible [[mass murder]]. [https://www.news.com.au/national/victoria/news/woman-three-kids-dead-in-melbourne-house-fire/news-story/f03587a1b8ed39f0b9441ac32aef8d98 (News.com.au)]
*[[Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**Two men who were photographed carrying [[plastic handcuffs|plastic hand restraints]] in the [[United States Senate chamber|Senate chamber]] during the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|storming]] of the [[United States Capitol]] are arrested in [[Tennessee]] and [[Texas]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/legal-issues/eric-munchel-larry-brock-arrested-capitol-zip-ties/2021/01/10/143b87cc-538f-11eb-a08b-f1381ef3d207_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*The [[Reserve Bank of New Zealand]] reveals that one of its [[file hosting service]]s storing "sensitive information" was [[Cyberattack|"maliciously" breached]]. The bank says the breach was contained and that they are investigating the "nature and extent" of "potentially accessed" information. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/434299/reserve-bank-likely-hacked-by-another-government-expert (Radio New Zealand)] [https://news.abs-cbn.com/business/01/10/21/new-zealand-central-bank-hit-by-cyber-attack (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
*Six inmates escape from a jail in California. Their whereabouts are unknown and being sought by California police. The six men are considered to be armed and dangerous. [https://wgntv.com/news/6-inmates-use-homemade-rope-to-escape-california-jail-authorities-say/ (WGNTV)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Kazakh legislative election]]
**[[Elections in Kazakhstan|Legislative elections]] are held in [[Kazakhstan]]. The election is criticized for a lack of opposition to the leading party [[Nur Otan]] and is therefore expected to be considered neither free nor fair by international observers. [https://www.rferl.org/a/kazakhstan-parliamentary-elections-2021/31040109.html (Radio Free Europe)] 
*[[2021 Kyrgyz presidential election]], [[2021 Kyrgyz referendum]]
**[[Elections in Kyrgyzstan|Presidential elections]] are held in [[Kyrgyzstan]] following last year's [[2020 Kyrgyzstani protests|political unrest]] and the resignation of [[President of Kyrgyzstan|President]] [[Sooronbay Jeenbekov]]. Interim [[Prime Minister of Kyrgyzstan|Prime Minister]] [[Sadyr Japarov]] is widely expected to win the election. The question of keeping the current [[parliamentary system]] or reintroducing a [[presidential system]] is also presented to the electorate in the form of a [[referendum]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-kyrgyzstan-election/nationalist-politician-likely-to-win-kyrgyz-presidential-vote-idUSKBN29F01T (Reuters)] [https://www.rferl.org/a/japarov-kyrgyzstan-presidential-election-referendum-/31040110.html (Radio Free Europe)]
*[[8th Congress of the Workers' Party of Korea]]
**[[North Korea]]n state media says that [[Kim Jong-un]] has been formally elected as the [[General Secretary of the_Workers' Party of Korea|General Secretary]] of the ruling [[Workers' Party of Korea]], inheriting the title from his late father [[Kim Jong-il]], who [[Death and state funeral of Kim Jong-il|died]] in 2011. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-northkorea-politics/north-korea-says-leader-kim-elected-as-general-secretary-of-ruling-party-kcna-idUSKBN29F0OD (Reuters)]
*[[2020–2021 Belarusian protests|2020-21 Belarusian protests]]
**[[President of Belarus|Belarusian President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] says that the [[Belarus|country]] will draft a [[Constitution of Belarus|new constitution]] by the end of the year. It remains unclear whether the new constitution will result in Lukashenko leaving office. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/lukashenko-promises-new-belarus-draft-constitution-by-end-of-the-year (''The Straits Times'')]
